categories.name: Journal
categories.description: Notes from the kitchen on fruit, batches and the counter.

posts.title: Figs, roasted until they split
posts.excerpt: How late-season figs are roasted on parchment until the skin splits, then folded through a chilled plum ripple.
posts.content:
Late-season figs arrive at Quay Lane in shallow crates, and Amara Okafor sorts them by hand before anything else happens. The ripest go to the table for the staff; the firm ones are halved onto parchment with the plums and roasted until the skin splits and the juice turns to syrup.

The roasted fruit is cooled overnight in the same cold-store where the bases rest. In the morning Ines Varga folds it through the chilled plum sorbet ripple by hand, so that every scoop of Burnt Fig & Plum carries a streak of fruit rather than an even sweetness.

It is one of six flavours churned on each open day, and it is served at −12 °C, the same temperature as every other tin on the slab.

posts.title: Rolling cones before noon
posts.excerpt: Sofie Brandt rolls wafer cones by hand on the warm iron each morning before the counter opens at noon.
posts.content:
Before the first tin is levelled, Sofie Brandt is at the warm iron by the back door. Each wafer is poured, pressed, lifted and rolled around a wooden form within a few seconds, while it is still soft enough to bend.

The cones are stacked on a rack to cool and are used the same day. Whatever is not used by close is set aside for the staff or discarded, which is the same rule we keep for the gelato itself.

The counter opens at 12:00, Wednesday to Sunday. If you arrive early you can usually watch the last cones come off the iron.
